readout_other: Craving and drug-use outcomes; MR thermometry monitoring of target-site temperature; neurological/behavioral/imaging assessment for adverse events
direction_notes: This is a letter clarifying technical/safety parameters and the circumstances of a reported serious adverse event (brain injury) during an FDA Significant-Risk trial of FUS neuromodulation for severe opioid use disorder; it does not itself report a new assessment of neuromodulation direction. Cited prior work from the same program reported 'clinically significant reductions in cravings and drug use.'
safety_notes: A brain injury occurred in one patient treated at 90 W for 389 s (below the study's allowed maximum of 100 W / 30 min); the manufacturer estimates in-situ peak rarefactional pressures of 1.3-2.4 MPa (free-field water equivalent 2.1-3.5 MPa) with mechanical index values above the range generally considered nonsignificant risk. Following the event, enhanced acoustic-feedback monitoring, sonication stopping criteria, and power modulation were implemented; 11 further participants have since been treated safely. The authors hypothesize that patient-specific elevated CO2 may have lowered the threshold for endogenous cavitation in this case, which is under active preclinical investigation; prior halts in other participants were not associated with neurological, behavioral, or imaging changes, and MR thermometry showed no temperature increase at the target.

exposures.label: Insightec 220 kHz FUS neuromodulation (opioid use disorder trial)

timing.protocol_description: Typical parameters were 220 kHz, emitted power 80-100 W, with a pulse pattern of 100 ms and 27% duty cycle spread across 8 sub-targets (3.3% duty cycle per spot). Sonication is delivered in up to six 5-minute treatment blocks with real-time acoustic-feedback monitoring and automatic safety halts; the study's allowed maximum was 100 W for up to 30 minutes. In the reported adverse-event case, the patient was treated at 90 W for 389 seconds.

flags.reason: The letter gives only approximate/partial cumulative counts for the broader trial ('more than 35 patients' treated before the safety-measure update, and '11 participants' treated after), plus the single adverse-event case; no single total for the specific protocol described is stated.

This letter (a technical/safety clarification correspondence) never names the anatomical target in its own text; cited companion papers targeted the nucleus accumbens for substance use disorder, but that is not stated here, so target is left unspecified.

The manufacturer's statement gives a '100 ms' pulse pattern together with a 27% duty cycle, but does not state whether 100 ms is the pulse duration or the repetition period; burst-rule ambiguity could not be resolved, so pulse duration and PRF are left not_reported and both numbers are given in protocol_description.
See pulse_duration_ms flag: the '100 ms' figure's role (pulse duration vs. period) is ambiguous, so PRF is left not_reported.

The manufacturer also reports a separate RMS-pressure estimate (theoretical 1.5-2.5 MPa, real-life 0.9-1.7 MPa) distinct from the peak rarefactional pressures (2.1-3.5 MPa water / 1.3-2.4 MPa in situ) used here; both metrics are given in the text, described in protocol_description/safety_notes.

Classified as 'derating' because the in-situ estimate is derived from the free-field/theoretical value adjusted by an empirical 60-70% factor from manufacturer experience, rather than a per-patient acoustic simulation.
This letter does not describe the trial's control/sham arm (or state whether one exists); coded as other pending that information.
The letter's purpose is safety/technical clarification of an adverse event, not a report of neuromodulation efficacy or direction; coded not_assessed.
